Hyperbilirubinemia is a frequent occurrence in patients taking atazanavir, including pregnant women. 4. Patients with underlying hepatitis B or C infections or significant transaminase elevations are at increased risk for further hepatic complications, including transaminase elevations or hepatic decompensation. 5. Chronic kidney disease has been reported in HIV-infected patients treated with atazanavir, with or without ritonavir. Consider alternative therapies for patients at high risk for renal disease or with preexisting renal conditions. 6. Renal laboratory testing, including serum creatinine, estimated creatinine clearance, and urinalysis with microscopic examination, should be conducted prior to initiating therapy and continued during treatment. 7. Cases of nephrolithiasis and/or cholelithiasis have been reported during postmarketing surveillance in patients receiving atazanavir. 8. Immune reconstitution syndrome has been reported in patients treated with combination antiretroviral therapy (ART). This may manifest as an inflammatory response to residual opportunistic infections, such as Mycobacterium avium, CMV, Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, or tuberculosis, necessitating further evaluation and treatment. 9. Autoimmune disorders, including Graves' disease, polymyositis, autoimmune hepatitis, and Guillain-Barré syndrome, have also been reported in the context of immune reconstitution. 10. Redistribution or accumulation of body fat, such as central obesity, dorsocervical fat enlargement (buffalo hump), peripheral wasting, facial wasting, breast enlargement, and a cushingoid appearance, has been observed in patients receiving ART. 11. New-onset diabetes mellitus, exacerbation of preexisting diabetes, and hyperglycemia have been reported in HIV-infected patients receiving protease inhibitors. 12. Atazanavir prolongs the PR interval on the electrocardiogram in both healthy subjects and those with HIV-1 infection. While atrioventricular (AV) conduction abnormalities are generally asymptomatic and limited to first-degree AV block, cases of second-degree AV block and other conduction abnormalities have been reported. 13. Cases of Stevens-Johnson syndrome, erythema multiforme, and toxic skin eruptions, including drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), have been reported. Mild-to-moderate maculopapular skin eruptions have also been observed in clinical trials and generally did not lead to treatment discontinuation. 14. Pregnant women taking atazanavir in combination with nucleoside analogues have reported cases of lactic acidosis syndrome, which can be fatal. Nucleoside analogues are associated with an increased risk of lactic acidosis syndrome. 15. All infants, including neonates exposed to atazanavir in utero, should be monitored for severe hyperbilirubinemia during the first few days of life. 16. Atazanavir is not recommended for use during pregnancy and should not be initiated in pregnant individuals. An alternative regimen is advised for those who become pregnant during therapy. 17. Components of the drug combination may interact with certain oral contraceptives. Nonhormonal forms of contraception should be considered. 18. The CDC recommends that HIV-infected mothers in the United States avoid breastfeeding to prevent postnatal transmission of HIV to their infants. 19. It is unknown whether atazanavir or cobicistat is secreted in human milk. 20. Cobicistat decreases estimated creatinine clearance by inhibiting tubular secretion of creatinine without affecting actual renal glomerular function. 21. Store tablets at 25°C (77°F), with excursions permitted to 15-30°C (59-86°F). 22. When co-administering with H2-receptor antagonists or proton-pump inhibitors, separate doses by at least 2 hours. 23. Patients with hemophilia types A and B treated with HIV protease inhibitors have reported increased bleeding, including spontaneous skin hematomas and hemarthrosis. 25. Cases of lactic acidosis syndrome, sometimes fatal, and symptomatic hyperlactatemia have occurred in pregnant women using atazanavir in combination with nucleoside analogues. 26.
